Name_Class: Rombocin A (Nisin variant, natural AMPs; lantibiotic, type 1, class 1 bacteriocin, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; XXW3, UCSS1b; BBW; BBMm)
Source: Romboutsia sedimentorum
Additional_Info: Discovery: genome mining with antiSMASH and BAGEL4. Biosynthetic gene cluster: romA: the precursor peptide; romBTC: biosynthetic genes; romRK: regulatory genes; romFEG: immunity genes, romP: maturation protease.Chemical modification: 3 amino acids dehydrated (XXW): T2, S5, and T18; four thiether rings (XXT): 3 and 8, 8 and 11, 13 and 19, and 21 and 24.Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this peptide is similar (54.84%) tonisin UThis peptide differs from nisin A by five amino acids, viz, P9A, K2I, A15V, L16I, and G18T, all located in rings B and C.Activity: inhibition zone: active against L. monocytogenes. MIC measured: L. lactis MG1363 (MIC 0.78 ug/ml), L. monocytogenes LMG10470 or TT82E or LK132 (MIC 12.5-25 ug/ml), B. cereus CH-85 (MIC 25 ug/ml), S. aureus LMG10147 or LMG15975 MRSA (MIC 100 ug/ml), and E. faecium LMG11423 or LMG16003 or LMG16216 (MIC 50-100 ug/ml) anti-VRE.Structure: A structure similar to nisin A was proposed with lipid II binding domain at the N-terminus and a pore-forming domain at the C-terminus. Diffrent from numerous known nisins collected in the APD, however, this peptide is unique since it contains only four thioether rings due to a shorter sequence. The lack of ring 5 may be the main reason for reduced activity compared to nisin Z.MOA:bacteria: like nisin, this short peptide also binds to lipid II.Recombinant production:bacteria:Lactococcus lactis: nisBTC is first induced by Zn2+ to hydrate the peptide and Rombocin A was then induced by adding nisin. NisC is required to make the thioether rings.Peptide stability: (1) stable for 5.5 h at pH 2-10 (more stable than nisin at pH 7); (2) stable between 22-50oC; more stable to proteases (trypsin, chymotrysin, and proteinase K) than nisin Z. These features make rombocin a promising candidate to be engineered into a new food preservative.SAR: the following changes (A9P, M20NMK, and K25A) reduced peptide activity, while a change I12 to K (I12K) increase peptide activity. The I12K mutant is called Rombocin K (see next APD entry).Est.Jan2024;
Title: Rombocin, a Short Stable Natural Nisin Variant, Displays Selective Antimicrobial Activity against Listeria monocytogenes and Employs a Dual Mode of Action to Kill Target Bacterial Strains.
Author: Guo L, Wambui J, Wang C, Broos J, Stephan R, Kuipers OP. 2024

Name_Class: Surotomycin (CB-183,315, synthetic AMPs, daptomycin analog, lactone, lipopeptide, depsipeptide, XXJ; UCSB1b)
Source: Library screen of daptomycin analogs with diffeetnt acyl chains
Additional_Info: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (92.31%) todaptomycin. D: 23%. This peptide shares the same sequence with daptomycin. To distinguish the two, the last residue was represented with Y in daptomycin but A here.Chemical modification: The natural form is cyclic due to the ester bond between the hydroxyl of T4 and the carboxyl of 3-anthraniloyl-L-alanine (represented with A here). In addition, the N-terminus is lipidated with an aromatic and unsaturated bond containing moiety. Other nonstandard amino acids include ornithine-6 (represented with K), (2S,3R)-3-methyl-glutamic acid-12 (represented with E), and three D-amino acids at positions N2, A8, and S11.Activity: active against C. difficile strains (MIC 0.06-4 ug/ml; MIC50 1 ug/ml; MIC90 2 ug/ml).SAR: a series of lipid tail has been tested with activity against C. difficile (MIC90 0.5-16 ug/ml), S. aureus ATCC 29213 (MIC 0.125-2 ug/ml) and activity variation was observed against E. faecalis 4->32 ug/ml). Hence, shortening the tail by one carbon (3t) reduced potency against C. difficile and the other tested strains. The phenyl alkyl tail 3p gave the optimal activity at 0.5 ug/ml (Yin et al., 2015).Animal model:hamster: survival study: oral daily for 5 days: Surotomycin demonstrated superior in vivo efficacy compared with other analogues when tested in the CDAD hamster model. It fully protected the animals at 0.5 mg/kg.Clinical trials:NCTNCT01598311 Phase II: CB-183,315 successfully completed a phase 2 clinical trial and was demonstrated to be safe and well tolerated in patients with C. difficile infection. In 2020, two phase 3 study was also conducted (NCT01597505 and NCT01598311): oral surotomycin (250 mg twice daily) to treat C. difficile infection (CDI) involving different populations (Cheknis et al., 2020).
Title: In vitro and in vivo characterization of CB-183,315, a novel lipopeptide antibiotic for treatment of Clostridium difficile.
